data.description:
## Context / Problem
The packaged author guide tells plan authors to name a rejected alternative, while the generated authoritative G6 criterion explicitly says not to require a rejected-alternatives section because it negatively primes implementers. This makes any deterministic clarity check for alternatives unsafe and gives authors contradictory instructions.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md
- examples or tests that pin the packaged guide wording

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The author guide matches the authoritative G6 contract: require a positive rationale for the chosen approach and do not require rejected-alternative prose; verified by comparing `rebar explain plan` with `rebar explain G6`.
- [ ] The minimum viable plan example and explanatory note no longer teach the conflicting rejected-alternative requirement; verified by a focused guide-content test or exact text inspection.
data.title: Plan author guide contradicts G6 anti-priming rule on rejected alternatives
